1.1.1.how: Check every image, icon, chart and control has a text alternative that serves the same purpose; purely decorative ones use alt="".
1.1.1.absent: no images, SVG, canvas, media or embeds detected
1.1.1.follow_up: axe checks that alt text exists, not that it is meaningful - read each one.

1.2.1.how: Prerecorded audio-only needs a transcript; prerecorded video-only needs a transcript or an audio description.
1.2.1.absent: no audio, video or embeds detected

1.2.2.how: Prerecorded video with sound needs synchronized captions.
1.2.2.follow_up: axe checks a captions track exists; confirm the captions are accurate and synchronized.

1.2.3.how: Prerecorded video needs an audio description or a full text alternative.

1.2.4.how: Live audio/video streams need live captions.
1.2.4.absent: no audio, video or embeds detected

1.2.5.how: Prerecorded video needs an audio description track.

1.3.1.how: Check that visual structure (headings, lists, tables, form groups, landmarks) is real markup, not just styling.
1.3.1.follow_up: axe checks markup validity, not whether the structure matches what is shown.

1.3.2.how: Check the reading order makes sense with CSS off or in a screen reader (DOM order matches visual order).

1.3.3.how: Check instructions don't rely only on shape, size, position or sound ("click the round button").

1.3.4.how: Rotate the device or resize the viewport: content must not be locked to one orientation.

1.3.5.how: Fields collecting personal data (name, email, address, ...) need the matching autocomplete value.
1.3.5.follow_up: axe checks autocomplete values are valid, not that every personal-data field has one.

1.4.1.how: Check information isn't conveyed by color alone (errors, required fields, chart series, links in text).
1.4.1.follow_up: axe checks links inside text blocks, not other color-only cues.

1.4.2.how: Audio that plays automatically for more than 3 seconds needs a pause/stop or its own volume control.

1.4.3.how: Check text over images, gradients and video, which axe cannot measure.
1.4.3.follow_up: axe measures plain text on plain backgrounds; check text over images and gradients by eye.

1.4.4.how: Zoom the browser to 200%: nothing should be lost, clipped or overlapping.
1.4.4.follow_up: axe checks the viewport meta tag doesn't block zooming; zoom to 200% to confirm.

1.4.5.how: Text should be real text, not text baked into images (logos excepted).
1.4.5.absent: no images, SVG or canvas detected

1.4.10.how: At 320px wide (400% zoom) content should reflow with no horizontal scrolling.

1.4.11.how: UI components (input borders, icons, focus rings) and meaningful graphics need 3:1 contrast.

1.4.12.how: Override text spacing (line 1.5, paragraph 2x, letter 0.12em, word 0.16em): nothing may be clipped or overlap.
1.4.12.follow_up: axe checks for inline spacing that blocks overrides; apply the spacing and look.

1.4.13.how: Content shown on hover or focus (tooltips, menus) must be dismissible, hoverable and persistent.
1.4.13.absent: no tooltip or popup triggers detected

2.1.1.how: Operate everything with the keyboard alone: links, buttons, menus, widgets and custom controls.
2.1.1.follow_up: axe checks some cases (e.g. scrollable regions); tab through the whole page.

2.1.2.how: Tab into and out of every widget (modals, embeds, editors): keyboard focus must never get trapped.

2.1.4.how: If the page defines single-key shortcuts, users must be able to turn them off or remap them.
2.1.4.reason: only applies if the page defines single-character keyboard shortcuts, which can't be detected automatically

2.2.1.how: Time limits (session timeouts, auto-refresh) must be adjustable, extendable or removable.
2.2.1.absent: no meta refresh detected (session timeouts can't be detected from the page)

2.2.2.how: Moving, blinking or auto-updating content lasting over 5 seconds needs a pause, stop or hide control.
2.2.2.absent: no animation or autoplaying media detected

2.3.1.how: Nothing should flash more than three times in any one second.
2.3.1.absent: no animation, video, canvas or embeds detected

2.4.1.how: A skip link or landmarks let keyboard users bypass repeated blocks.
2.4.1.follow_up: axe checks a bypass mechanism exists; confirm the skip link works and is reachable by keyboard.

2.4.2.how: The page title should describe its topic or purpose.
2.4.2.follow_up: axe checks a title exists; confirm it is descriptive.

2.4.3.how: Tab through the page: focus order must follow a logical, meaningful sequence.

2.4.4.how: Each link's purpose must be clear from its text or context (avoid bare "click here" / "read more").
2.4.4.follow_up: axe checks links have text, not that the text is meaningful.

2.4.5.how: Users should have more than one way to find pages (navigation, search, sitemap).
2.4.5.reason: a site-level check - it needs more than one page

2.4.6.how: Headings and labels must describe their topic or purpose.

2.4.7.how: Tab through the page: the focused element must always have a visible focus indicator.

2.4.11.how: Focused elements must not be completely hidden by sticky headers, footers or cookie banners.
2.4.11.absent: no fixed or sticky elements detected

2.5.1.how: Anything done with multi-finger or path-based gestures (pinch, swipe, drawing) also needs a single-pointer alternative.
2.5.1.absent: no canvas, custom widgets, draggable items or embeds detected

2.5.2.how: Actions should fire on pointer release, and be cancellable by moving the pointer away first.

2.5.3.how: A control's accessible name must contain its visible label text.
2.5.3.absent: no controls with an aria-label detected

2.5.4.how: Actions triggered by shaking or tilting the device also need a normal control, and motion must be switch-off-able.
2.5.4.reason: only applies if the page responds to device motion, which can't be detected automatically

2.5.7.how: Anything done by dragging needs a single-pointer alternative (click or tap).
2.5.7.absent: no draggable elements or custom widgets detected

2.5.8.how: Pointer targets should be at least 24x24 CSS pixels, or have enough spacing.
2.5.8.follow_up: axe checks target size for the rendered layout; confirm at other viewport sizes.

3.1.1.how: The page's lang attribute must match its actual language.
3.1.1.follow_up: axe checks lang exists and is valid; confirm it is the right language.

3.1.2.how: Passages in a different language need their own lang attribute.
3.1.2.follow_up: axe checks lang values are valid, not that foreign passages are marked up.

3.2.1.how: Focusing an element must not trigger a change of context (navigation, pop-up, focus jump).

3.2.2.how: Changing a form control's value must not submit or navigate unexpectedly.

3.2.3.how: Navigation should appear in the same order on every page.
3.2.3.reason: a site-level check - compare several pages

3.2.4.how: Components with the same function must be labelled the same way across pages.
3.2.4.reason: a site-level check - compare several pages

3.2.6.how: Where help is offered (contact link, chat, FAQ) it must appear in the same relative place on every page.
3.2.6.reason: a site-level check - compare several pages

3.3.1.how: Submit invalid or empty input: errors must be shown in text and identify the field in error.
3.3.1.absent: no forms or form controls detected

3.3.2.how: Fields need visible labels or instructions (format hints, required marks).
3.3.2.follow_up: axe checks fields have accessible names; confirm the visible labels and instructions are clear.

3.3.3.how: When an input error is detected and a fix is known, the message should suggest it.
3.3.3.absent: no forms or form controls detected

3.3.4.how: Submissions that are legal, financial or change user data must be reversible, checked or confirmed.

3.3.7.how: In a multi-step process, information already entered must not have to be entered again.
3.3.7.reason: a flow-level check - walk through the multi-step process

3.3.8.how: Logging in must not require a cognitive test (memorising, transcribing, puzzles); allow paste and password managers.
3.3.8.absent: no password field or CAPTCHA detected

4.1.1.how: Markup must be well-formed: unique IDs and correct nesting.

4.1.2.how: Custom widgets need the correct name, role and state (expanded, checked, ...) exposed to assistive technology.
4.1.2.follow_up: axe checks ARIA validity; test custom widgets with a screen reader.

4.1.3.how: Status messages (success, errors, result counts) must be announced via role=status/alert or live regions without moving focus.
4.1.3.absent: no live regions or forms detected
